relationship.statement: A simple pendulum's swing period depends only on its length and gravity, increasing with the square root of length. Bob mass cancels out because weight and inertia scale together, while small starting angles change swing width and peak speed without changing the period.
assumptions: Restoring torque is approximated using small angles, where sin(theta) is close to theta in radians.
Gravity is fixed at Earth surface value g = 9.81 m/s2, and the rod is massless and rigid.
Air drag and pivot friction are zero, so each pendulum keeps a constant amplitude.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var refL = 1.0; var refM = 2.0; var refThetaDeg = 15; var refPivotX = -0.85; var testPivotX = 0.85; var forceScale = 0.20; var degToRad = Math.PI / 180; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var thetaDeg = inputs.angle; var thetaRad = thetaDeg * degToRad; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var period = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var angleRad = thetaRad * Math.cos(omega * t); var testAngle = thetaDeg * Math.cos(omega * t); var testX = testPivotX + L * Math.sin(angleRad); var testY = -L * Math.cos(angleRad); var weight = m * g; var peakAccel = g * thetaRad; var testForceY = testY - forceScale * m; var testBobSize = 0.20 + 0.75 * (m - 1.0) / 3.0; var refOmega = Math.sqrt(g / refL); var refPeriod = 2 * Math.PI / refOmega; var refThetaRad = refThetaDeg * degToRad; var refAngleRad = refThetaRad * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var refAngle = refThetaDeg * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var refX = refPivotX + refL * Math.sin(refAngleRad); var refY = -refL * Math.cos(refAngleRad); var refForceY = refY - forceScale * refM; var refBobSize = 0.20 + 0.75 * (refM - 1.0) / 3.0; var sameLength = Math.abs(L - refL) < 0.05; var sameLenDiffMass = sameLength && Math.abs(m - refM) > 0.1; var sameLenDiffAngle = sameLength && Math.abs(thetaDeg - refThetaDeg) > 0.5; var longerRod = L > refL + 0.05; return { period: period, refPeriod: refPeriod, weight: weight, peakAccel: peakAccel, testAngle: testAngle, refAngle: refAngle, testX: testX, testY: testY, refX: refX, refY: refY, testForceY: testForceY, refForceY: refForceY, testBobSize: testBobSize, refBobSize: refBobSize, sameLenDiffMass: sameLenDiffMass, sameLenDiffAngle: sameLenDiffAngle, sameLength: sameLength, longerRod: longerRod }; }

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum's swing?
lesson.description: Compare an adjustable pendulum with a fixed 1.0 m reference as they swing side by side. Vary length, mass, and release angle to watch which controls shift the period on the plot.
lesson.instructions: Set Test length to 1.0 m to match the reference period, then vary Test mass and Release angle to verify that neither shifts the cycle timing. Next, change Test length above and below 1.0 m while watching the live period readout and the angle-time waves drift out of step.
lesson.goal: Only rod length and gravity set a simple pendulum's small-angle period; mass cancels out of restoring acceleration, while release angle changes arc width and speed without altering timing.
